newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: HSBC deal boosts Argentine Roberts expansion plans.
newsitem.headline: HSBC deal boosts Argentine Roberts expansion plans.

text.p: The purchase of Argentina's Grupo Roberts by HSBC Holdings Plc will boost the Argentine group's core financial and service businesses, top Roberts officials said Friday.

"It will enable us to improve our position in the four sectors of our core business: banking, insurance, health care and pension funds," Enrique Ruete, President of Grupo Roberts executive committee, told a press conference.

"It will enhance even more the group's dynamics," he added after HSBC announced in London that it would buy all the share capital of Grupo Roberts, a holding company that includes Banco Roberts, for between $600 and $688 million. HSBC already had a 29.9 percent in Banco Roberts.
Ruete said local management will remain in charge and there will be no immediate change of brand name, with the possible later addition of the group's "HSBC" trademark to that of Roberts.

He added Banco Roberts ranks among Argentina's top eight or nine banks as considered by assets or deposits, second or third in the general insurance sector and second or third in health care services. It also ranks in second place in the pension sector with 957,000 affiliates and has a minority 12 percent of textile and footwear company Alpargatas.
The HSBC deal will accelerate Banco Roberts' plans to widen its banking services for major corporates, medium-to-small firms and consumers, Ruete said.

The group's Executive Director Jorge Heinze said Banco Roberts would push ahead with a plan to increase its current 63 branches at a rate of at least six new branches per year "and possibly more than that."
He added the HSBC deal meant Grupo Roberts was dropping plans announced last month to launch this year an initial public offering of between $100 million and $150 million.
Ruete said Banco Roberts would benefit from synergies with Bamerindus, Brazil's third or four largest bank, which HSBC bought in March for about $1.0 billion.
"HSBC will back synergies with Brazil not only with a capital injection but also with technology," he said.

"The fact we are so well positioned in both countries will enable us to get an important portion of the foreign trade," Ruete said, adding there would also be benefits from synergies in the insurance business as Bamerindus is also Brazil's fith largest insurance company.
The purchase of Banco Roberts capped a buying spree of Argentine banks by foreign banks this month.

Spain's Banco Santander bought this week 35.06 percent of Banco Rio for $594 million with an option to buy another 15 percent. The first stake involves voting control. Two weeks before Spain's Banco de Bilbao Vizcaya bought 71.8 percent of Banco Frances for $466 million.
Those deals left Banco de Galicia as Argentina's only major private bank in local hands.
HSBC signed in March an option to buy 19.9 percent of Banca Serfin, Mexico's third largest bank, for $300 million.
Also in March it bought a 10 percent stake in Banco del Sur del Peru (Bancosur), Peru's seventh largest retail bank. It already has a four percent stake in Chile's Banco de Santiago.
Asked whether HSBC was planning any new purchase in Latin America, its local representative Marcos Brujis said: "Before eating dinner we have to digest lunch."
